scope: Telangana & Andhra Pradesh (architected to extend to all Indian states without schema change)

datasets_blocked.name: revenue_division (Andhra Pradesh)
datasets_blocked.reason: Only available source is self-flagged stale, internally inconsistent (row sum ≠ stated total), and confirmed missing at least one real division

datasets_blocked.name: mandal (both states)
datasets_blocked.reason: Every primary source attempt was robots.txt-blocked or failed on fetch; the one available secondary compilation lost its table structure on extraction
datasets_blocked.unblock_requires: LGD sub-district bulk export, or Census 2011/Telangana Statistical Abstract PDF, obtained via manual download and uploaded for direct parsing

dependencies: This package has no upstream package dependencies — it is the root of the entire ValueWeave dataset dependency graph. All future packages (Education Foundation, Industrial Infrastructure, Industries & Products, Skills & Training, Companies & MSMEs, Government Schemes, Manufacturing Knowledge, Supply Chain, Knowledge Graph Relationships) depend on this package's state/district (and eventually mandal) tables for geographic anchoring.

knowledge_graph_coverage.coverage_note: 138 nodes / 136 edges are graph-load-ready today. Full Geography Foundation package scope (incl. Mandal, Village, ULBs, Industrial Parks, Infrastructure, Water/Natural Resources) is estimated at several thousand additional nodes once all queued datasets are populated.

ai_readiness_score.methodology: Weighted: provenance completeness (every row has data_source/source_url/confidence_score/verification_status = 100%, weight 30%) + stable identifiers (UUID PKs + immutable ref codes = 100%, weight 20%) + geo-precision (lat/long populated = 0%, weight 20%) + cross-government-ID linkage (LGD codes populated = 0%, weight 15%) + FK integrity where data exists (100%, weight 15%). Computed: 0.30(100)+0.20(100)+0.20(0)+0.15(0)+0.15(100) = 65.
ai_readiness_score.interpretation: The package is fully AI-consumable in structure (an AI system can reliably reason about what it knows, doesn't know, and how confident to be) but is missing the geo-spatial and cross-government-ID layers that would let it plug into external systems (e.g., matching against GIS map layers or other LGD-keyed datasets).
